source: Field list from DCADS/2004/FY2004_agency_record_layout.pdf, 'DD Form 350 extract', which gives field order, type and width but no byte positions because the file is delimited. The FY2005 and FY2006 layout PDFs are image-only with no text layer and could not be extracted; they are covered here on the evidence that all three years carry the same 88 fields at the same widths and that the geography, dollar and date columns decode correctly in each.

notes.format: Exclamation-mark delimited and simultaneously FIXED WIDTH. Every record is 601 characters in FY2004 and FY2006 and 603 in FY2005, and the delimiters sit at identical byte positions in every well-formed record: one pattern across all 694,119 clean FY2004 records, all 1,357,166 FY2005 records and all 1,272,615 FY2006 records, with no variants. Parsing is therefore by byte offset, from delimiter_offsets below, not by splitting on the delimiter. Splitting discards that structure and turns a record that has lost one delimiter into either a silent field shift or a dropped record.
notes.trailing_delimiter: Each record ends with a delimiter after the last field, so splitting a line yields 89 pieces of which the 89th is empty or holds the stray carriage return of the CRLF terminator. Only the first 88 are fields. This is why a naive delimiter count suggests one more field than the layout lists.
notes.signed_dollars: Dollars carry an explicit leading sign, for example '+000000048416', rather than the trailing zoned-decimal sign of every earlier era, so decode_zoned does not apply here.
notes.not_applicable: A single hyphen in any field means non-applicable or not reported, per the layout note.
notes.geography: Arranged differently from the fixed-width eras: state_code is the 2-digit FIPS state and county_fips the 3-digit FIPS county, held separately rather than concatenated, so the 5-digit identifier is state_code plus county_fips. contractor_state is a postal abbreviation describing the contractor address, not the place of performance.
notes.lumpsum: No id_key exists in this era, so DD1057 lump-sum rows cannot be identified and is_lumpsum is 0 throughout. Whether the web-format extract includes below-threshold tallies at all is open; the dollar totals against FY2003 are the way to settle it.
notes.month_key: Six digits, CCYYMM in form, but the last two digits are a FISCAL month, not a calendar one: 01 is October and 12 is September. The source layout labels this 'Fiscal reporting period, yyyymm', which invites reading 200401 as January 2004 when it is October 2003. Verified on all 23 month_key-bearing fiscal years: fiscal month 01 carries action dates in the preceding October, 04 in January, 12 in September, without exception. Characters three and four still give the fiscal year. Reading the month as calendar shifts the whole era by one quarter, so dcads_common.derive_time_columns emits calendar_yearmonth and nobody should re-derive it. Note also that this is the REPORTING period and lags the obligation: only 39% to 70% of a month's records share its modal action month, so anything needing when the money was obligated must key on action_date.
notes.month_key_defect: 8 FY2006 records carry '073106', which is MMDDYY for 31 July 2006 rather than CCYYMM. All 8 are Navy (1700) with action dates inside FY2006 totalling $395,327, so they belong in fy2006. The parser falls back to the fiscal year implied by action_date and flags them in month_key_repaired. FY2004 and FY2005 contain no malformed month_key.
notes.anomalies: 290 FY2004 records deviate from the canonical delimiter pattern, in four groups, each group sharing one exact signature. In every one of them the first byte position that moves is 396, the end of field 34 (fsc_description), so fields 0 to 33 - including dollars, state_code, county_fips, the dates and the contract number - are at canonical offsets and read correctly with no remapping at all. FY2005 and FY2006 have no deviating records.
notes.field_documentation: Every field carries a label taken from the FY2004 layout, and a dd350_item giving the DD Form 350 item number where the layout prints one. Twelve fields have no item number in the source, being unnumbered continuation lines of the field above them, and are left without one.

offset_note: The two tables differ in exactly one field: n_actions is 4 wide in FY2004 and FY2006 and 6 wide in FY2005, which is the whole of the 601 against 603 record length. Every other field has identical width and position in all three years, which is the evidence behind covering FY2005 and FY2006 with the FY2004 field list.

imputed.basis: These are contract and contractor attributes that do not vary within a contract. Every one of them takes a single value across the undamaged FY2004 records of contract DAAA0902D0007, and the same contract recurs 293 times in FY2005 and 288 times in FY2006 agreeing on every value. Only fields whose recovered value is a real code are filled; place_of_manufacture and country_of_origin are blank in the source anyway, so filling them would turn null into empty string and add nothing. Applied ONLY when the record's contract_no matches, so the same delimiter signature appearing on a different contract leaves the fields null and is reported.

anomalies.diagnosis: fsc_description is written 65 characters wide instead of 50. The 15-character overrun is paid for by omitting canonical fields 62 to 68, whose widths total 8 characters plus 7 delimiters, so the record still occupies 601 bytes and only the delimiter count changes. The arithmetic closes exactly.
anomalies.evidence: Derived by exhaustive search, not by hand: every single-absent-run map was scored on the 53 closed-domain code fields, taking their domains from the 694,119 clean records. This map is the unique best on (domain violations, width mismatches) with 0 violations and the one expected width mismatch, field 34 itself. Absent runs 61-67 and 65-71 both produce violations; 66-72 also gives 0 violations but needs a second width mismatch and so loses. Under the winning map premium_percent is '000', n_actions '0001', and nondod_agency and nondod_office are blank at their declared widths of 4 and 6, in all 228 records.

imputed.basis: Same contract and same basis as fsc_desc_65. This pattern omits three further fields, hubzone, ethnic_group and veteran_owned, all of which are blank across the same contract's undamaged records in all three fiscal years, so they stay null.

anomalies.diagnosis: The same defect one step further: fsc_description is written 70 wide instead of 50, and canonical fields 62 to 71 are omitted. Those widths total 11 characters plus 10 delimiters, 21 against a 20-character overrun, and the residual byte is absorbed as labor_standards being written 2 wide rather than 1.
anomalies.evidence: Same exhaustive search as fsc_desc_65. Unique best with 0 domain violations against 8 or more for every other absent run, and the only two width mismatches are the expected ones: field 34's overrun and the 2-wide labor_standards that absorbs the residual byte.

anomalies.diagnosis: The delimiter between premium_percent (D4C) and sbir (D7) is omitted, fusing them into one 4-character field such as '010A'. Every field after it shifts one byte left and a single pad character appears at end of line. These records still split into exactly 88 pieces, so they passed the old length guard and were written with a silently shifted tail: nondod_office held n_actions' value and n_actions was null.
anomalies.evidence: The tail width signature 4/6/4/1 pins the last four fields, and every remapped value falls inside the domain observed across the 694,119 clean records. The competing map, which would treat premium_percent as 4 wide, puts M/P/R/S/U into demo_program (observed domain blank/N/Y) and Y into subcontracting_plan (blank/A/B/C/D), and is rejected.

imputed.basis: sbir is 'A' across all 7 undamaged FY2004 records of contract DACW0102C0019 and all 13 of its FY2005 records, with no other value anywhere. Applied only when contract_no matches.

anomalies.diagnosis: sbir (D7) is absent along with its delimiter. Every field after it is written one position earlier than the canonical layout would put it, and the two bytes that frees appear as padding at end of line. Like premium_pct_fused these records split into exactly 88 pieces and so passed the old length guard, and were written with a silently shifted tail.
anomalies.evidence: 0 domain violations and 0 width mismatches, uniquely among the single-absent-run candidates that fit the widths; the next-best, treating demo_program as the absent field, puts 17 out-of-domain values into subcontracting_plan. Note that the delimiters here are canonical through byte 579, so a reading based on byte position alone would put fields 0 to 82 at their canonical indices and conclude cost_accounting_clause was the absent field. That reading was tried first and is WRONG: it assigns 'Y' to subcontracting_plan, whose domain over 694,119 clean records is blank/A/B/C/D, and 'M' to demo_program, whose domain is blank/N/Y. Position and content disagree here, and content wins, corroborated by premium_pct_fused carrying the identical field sequence from this point on.

fields.name: month_key
fields.label: Reporting period, CCYYMM in form, but the month is a FISCAL month: 01 is October and 12 is September. Not a calendar month, and not when the money was obligated: for that see action_date.

fields.name: action_date
fields.label: Date of action, yyyymmdd. When the action was OBLIGATED, which is not the reporting period: see month_key. The two agree on fiscal year for about 99% of records; they differ where reporting lagged the obligation.
